newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends firm on spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends firm on spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures shrugged off their earlier weak tone and ended firm on spillover support from other markets and on ongoing concern about possible flooding in the northern Plains, traders said.
"I think we just went with the flow of other markets -- except for the corn," an MGE floor source said.
Fund-buying in CBOT wheat lent support to MGE spring wheat, which had been weaker on ideas the market had closed too firm relative to other U.S. wheat markets Monday.
CBOT soybeans also added some spillover support as funds turned technical buyers late in that market.

Spring wheat was also prone to hedge pressure brought on by active farmer sales of wheat. Traders said many growers are unloading wheat now in anticipation of the tranportation snags that will result from the spring thaw.
MGE spring wheat settled steady to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with May up one cent at $4.01-3/4. July closed up 1-1/2 cents at $3.88-3/4.

Atwood/Peavey sold two million May bushels, and traders guessed that a good chunk of that sale was hedging related to country movement. Country Hedging also sold 1.2 million May. Linnco bought 1.6 million May.
MGE barley futures did not trade.
